items.followUp: A crane lifts a 150 kg load through 8 m in 12 s. Calculate its power, taking g = 10 m s⁻².

rubric.why: Power is work done per unit time; for lifting a mass, the work is mgh.
rubric.how: Award for stating P = W/t or the equivalent P = mgh/t.

rubric.why: The work calculation must use the mass, gravitational acceleration and height, and give work in joules.
rubric.how: Award for substituting the given values and obtaining 12000 J.

rubric.why: The calculated work must be divided by the time taken.
rubric.how: Award for evaluating 12000 J ÷ 10 s as 1200.

rubric.why: Power must be reported with its SI unit.

modelAnswer: Given: m = 200 kg, h = 6 m, t = 10 s, g = 10 m s⁻²
Work done, W = mgh = (200 kg)(10 m s⁻²)(6 m) = 12000 J
The power of the pump is 1200 W.

rubric.why: Mechanics is identified by the physical subjects it deals with.
rubric.how: Award for stating that mechanics is the branch of physics dealing with motion and forces.

rubric.why: Heat is described as energy transferred between bodies at different temperatures.
rubric.how: Award for stating that heat is energy transferred from a hotter body to a colder body.

modelAnswer: Mechanics is the branch of physics that deals with the motion of objects and the forces acting on them.
Heat is energy transferred from a hotter body to a colder body because of a temperature difference.

items.followUp: Can a car moving at constant speed around a circular track be accelerating? Explain.

rubric.why: A body can accelerate even if its speed remains constant.
A change in direction changes velocity and therefore produces acceleration.
rubric.how: Award for explaining that the changing direction changes velocity, so the body is accelerating.

modelAnswer: Yes, a body moving at constant speed can have acceleration.
If its direction changes, its velocity changes; therefore it is accelerating.

items.followUp: State two properties of a good thermometric substance.

rubric.why: Uniform expansion makes temperature readings consistent.
rubric.how: Award for stating that mercury expands uniformly with temperature.

rubric.why: Any one further suitable property explains why mercury is useful in thermometers.
rubric.how: Award for one additional valid reason, such as being shiny and visible, having a wide temperature range, not wetting glass, having high thermal conductivity, or having low specific heat.

modelAnswer: Mercury expands uniformly when its temperature changes, giving a reliable temperature scale.
It is shiny and easily visible in the thermometer tube.
It remains liquid over a wide range of temperatures and does not wet the glass.
